title: A lease on a resource
description:
A pool has a limited number of connections. A `Lease` object represents holding one of them: it takes a connection when it is created and gives it back automatically when it is destroyed. This idea (tying a resource to an object's lifetime) is the most important one in C++; it is called RAII and gets its own lesson later.

The `Pool` struct is provided. Write the class `Lease`:

- `explicit Lease(Pool& pool)`: if the pool has a free connection (`inUse < capacity`), take one (`++inUse`) and remember that this lease is valid. Otherwise the lease is not valid and takes nothing.
- `~Lease()`: give the connection back, but only if this lease actually holds one.
- `bool valid() const`.
hints: In the constructor, check `pool.inUse < pool.capacity`; only then increase `inUse` and set the lease to valid.
The destructor gives the connection back only if this lease actually took one: `if (m_valid) --m_pool.inUse;`.
